title: Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District features Republican incumbent Michael Guest seeking a fifth term against Democratic nominee Michael Chiaradio and Libertarian candidate Erik Kiehle. The district covers central and east-central Mississippi, including the Jackson suburbs and Meridian, with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+14. Guest, who chairs the House Ethics Committee and serves on the Homeland Security Committee, was forced into a 2022 primary runoff after voting for a bipartisan January 6 commission but has since consolidated Republican support. Chiaradio, a farmer and entrepreneur, is making his first run for public office on a platform of economic investment in rural communities and fiscal sustainability, while Kiehle advocates for America First policies and limited government as a third-party alternative.
polling_note: No public opinion polling was found for this race. The Cook Political Report rates Mississippi's 3rd District as 'Solid Republican' (as of February 2025), indicating the incumbent is heavily favored based on the district's partisan voting history.

candidates.name: Michael Guest
candidates.summary: Michael Guest is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2018. He chairs the House Committee on Ethics and serves on the House Homeland Security Committee. Before Congress, he served as district attorney for Mississippi's 20th Circuit Court District covering Rankin and Scott counties.

candidates.name: Michael A. Chiaradio
candidates.summary: Michael A. Chiaradio is a farmer and entrepreneur from Shubuta, Mississippi, running as the Democratic nominee for Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District. He raises livestock, holds an MBA from Felician University, and previously supervised teams supporting the Affordable Care Act at a global public company. Chiaradio's campaign focuses on intelligent public investment to drive rural economic competitiveness and fiscal responsibility.

candidates.name: Erik Kiehle
candidates.summary: Erik Kiehle is a Libertarian candidate running for U.S. House in Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District. A property manager and volunteer firefighter in Lauderdale County, he holds a BBA from the University of California, Riverside and previously worked as a Senior Support Engineer at Apple. His campaign emphasizes America First policies, fiscal conservatism, and opposition to foreign aid.
